title: LP2-15 prime gaps: does the modulo-28 tail repeat?
question: Do the supplied LP2-15 Fibonacci-indexed prime gaps repeat the final modulo-28 tail 8,20,10,6 under the same fixed generator?
summary: The supplied 16 primes and 15 gaps are arithmetically correct. The four-residue tail occurs once; the next generated gap is 4 modulo 28, rather than the predicted 8.

scope.representation: The user-supplied derived 4×4 prime matrix in source.json, checked against the established LP2-15 panel construction; not the printed panel values themselves.
scope.procedure: Verify the 16 Fibonacci-indexed primes and 15 shown gaps, count exact four-number tail occurrences, then extend the same generator by eight distinct Fibonacci prime indices and compare a fixed period-four prediction.
scope.parameters: Ascending spiral sequence; forward consecutive differences; modulus 28; exact tail 8,20,10,6; next eight indices 1597 through 46368; no phase or path search. Modulus 29 shown only as a declared comparison.
scope.exclusions: No alternate spiral path, reverse gaps, modulus optimization, rune mapping, key schedule, or manuscript ciphertext test.

finding: The shown 8,20,10,6 tail occurs exactly once at gap positions 12–15. The first continuation is 5660 mod 28 = 4, not 8; none of eight new residues matches the fixed period-four prediction at its position.
limitations: This rejects only the period-four continuation of the supplied arithmetic tail under the established Fibonacci prime-index generator. Modulus 28 is unexplained and no decoding rule was supplied; other panel-derived operations are outside this test.
next_steps: A different numerical or rune-key proposal needs a fixed traversal, modulus rationale, residue mapping, target text and held-out prediction before testing.

review.reviewer: Codex; independent sieve and source-matrix checker; human review pending
